ev-918e0fc568.rationale: Context-gated arrival family (#259, product redact-secret#701). Three sources describe a prefix-less <32 hex>-<8 hex>-<8 hex> value as Mailgun's newer private API key: a Mailgun-repository contributor (mailgun-go#72, 2019), customer reports (Discourse, 2018) and trufflehog#3870 (2025). Both pinned peers match the shape: gitleaks 8.30.1 mailgun-signing-key (keyword-gated, [a-h0-9]) and trufflehog 3.97.4 mailgun (its "Hex MailGun Token" pattern, chunk-keyword-gated). Mailgun documents no shape for any key, so no issued key is known and the contract is recorded uncertainty. Before this issue, the benchmark taxonomy listed the triplet as an unsupported legacy signing key; this issue corrects that reason. The triplet is recognised only beside a same-line mailgun keyword and scores as policy. Its twins keep the triplet and change only the context. The alphabet is lowercase hex, the intersection of both peers, so an uppercase triplet is a near-miss control rather than a twin.
